findings.text: follow-on: the rotation case's negative half was narrowed from `not _log_file(second).exists()` to `not (second / "logs" / (first_log.name + ".1")).exists()`, and the narrowed assertion holds for a reason unrelated to the mechanism: `_bound_server_log` (reckon/serve.py:314) rotates only an existing over-bound file, and the moved-to home never has a log to rotate in this case, so neither the landed code nor either mutated arm can make a predecessor appear there. The case still guards the rotation through its positive predecessor assertion at line 249 (proven by logs/negative-control-bound.log), but the plan's done-when clause that case (2) 'creates nothing in the second home' is no longer asserted by this case, and only case 1 now carries that direction. The trade-off is deliberate and documented in the commit and the inline comment, so it does not hold the node.
